themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 50 THIS WEEK, a 270% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 13.5 per week (z-score: 5.16), signaling a sudden environmental quality crisis affecting multiple blocks in Mott Haven/Melrose.
evidence: 50 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 13.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (270% spike)
Z-score of 5.16 indicates highly statistically significant deviation from baseline
Complaint type concentrated in outdoor/commercial zones, suggesting construction, vehicle traffic, or street-level activity
reporting_angles: Door-knock reporting: which blocks are seeing the most complaints; are residents losing sleep or unable to conduct business?
Source investigation: is this tied to a specific construction project, transit work, or commercial activity uptick?

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampment Emergencies
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK, a 300% increase over the 8-week average of 2.8 per week (z-score: 4.81), indicating a sharp rise in visible street homelessness that aligns with CB201's recurring budget request for expanded DHS services.
evidence: 11 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly baseline (300% spike, z-score: 4.81)
Community Board 201 has repeatedly requested additional DHS services for homeless populations across consecutive budget cycles—unsolved problem
Spike corresponds with winter months, suggesting seasonal pressure on shelter capacity
reporting_angles: Profile the geography: which parks, transit hubs, or commercial corridors are seeing the most encampments? Interview residents and business owners.
DHS capacity check: are shelters full? Why is street homelessness accelerating now? Interview agency officials and advocacy groups.

themes_detail.label: Lead Contamination Alert
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK, a 700% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.4 per week (z-score: 5.42), raising urgent public health concerns in a district with aging housing stock and repeated CB budget requests for building inspector expansion.
evidence: 3 lead complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community Board 201 has submitted recurring budget requests to expand DOB building inspector capacity—indicating chronic enforcement gaps
District 201 filed 279 alteration permits in last 90 days; lead risk likely in renovation work on older buildings
reporting_angles: Safety investigation: where are the lead complaints concentrated? Are they in rental buildings, schools, or daycare facilities? Who is at risk?
Enforcement gap: why is DOB understaffed in this district? How many buildings are overdue for lead inspections?

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicle Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 14 LAST WEEK, a 154% increase over the 8-week baseline of 5.5 per week (z-score: 6.01), suggesting accelerating street clutter and potential safety/environmental hazards in high-traffic residential areas.
evidence: 14 derelict vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (154% spike, z-score: 6.01)
Overlaps with broader streets/sanitation quality issues (sewer/root damage spike of 1233% and sanitation worker complaints up 1100%)
District has chronic illegal parking complaints (1,792 over 90 days), suggesting systemic street management challenges
reporting_angles: Visual reporting: document the streets with the most abandoned vehicles; map the concentration by block.
Process story: how does NYPD/Sanitation tow derelict vehicles? Are response times adequate? Why the sudden jump?

themes_detail.label: Sewer & Root Damage Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints spiked to 5 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1233% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.4 per week (z-score: 6.65), and sanitation worker complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK (1100% spike), pointing to acute infrastructure failure and service delivery breakdown.
evidence: 5 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (1233% spike, z-score: 6.65)
3 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Community Board 201 has submitted recurring requests to DEP to accelerate capital projects—unmet infrastructure need
reporting_angles: Investigation: which streets are seeing sidewalk collapse or sewer backups? Are residents dealing with water intrusion or sewage issues?
DEP accountability: what is the status of planned sewer/sidewalk repairs in CD201? Why are complaints spiking now?
